t.E482.agn: In 2013 EFSA set an ADI of 22 mg/kg body weight for E481 and E482, alone or in combination. Estimated exposure was found to be below the ADI in adults, including the elderly, and above the ADI at average levels in the other age groups and at high consumption in all groups.
t.E482.body: During digestion it is split into stearic acid and lactic acid; both occur naturally in foods and are part of the body's normal metabolism.
t.E482.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded
t.E482.eff.0.w: Age groups other than adults; all groups at high consumption
t.E482.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E482.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by reacting stearic acid with lactic acid and converting it into the calcium salt.
t.E482.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI of 22 mg/kg body weight for E481/E482; estimated exposure exceeds the ADI in some age groups.
t.E482.summary: An emulsifier produced from lactic acid and fatty acids. It is a dough improver in bread and bakery products.
t.E482.what: It is an emulsifier that strengthens dough and preserves softness; it improves the texture of bakery products.
